quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is not recommended because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be worn if the jacket is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: You should still wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from injury and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out so the group is easier to see.
Stay close together so the group is easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together so the group is easier to see.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but leave enough space around each rider to maneuver safely. Staying close together makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Do not ride in pairs because it does not leave enough room to move.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with your turn signals. If your left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing downward, it means you are slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a major cause of motorcycle crashes and deaths. Studies show that nearly 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle accidents had been drinking.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, all of the following are important, except:
questions.explanation: To get the best protection, choose a helmet that meets DOT standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no visible damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The side nearest the passing vehicle is safer.
You will feel a strong wind blast from the passing vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This might encourage the driver to return to your lane before it is actually safe to do so.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, you should stay at least ______ behind another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, stay at least two seconds behind another vehicle. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a cause of motorcycle wobble?
questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not speed up to try to stop a wobble.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow all rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: A helmet should not:
questions.explanation: For the best protection, your helmet should meet DOT and state standards, fit snugly all the way around, and have no visible damage. Replace any helmet that was worn during a crash.

questions.question: Your street-legal motorcycle must have all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: A street-legal motorcycle must have at least: a headlight, taillight, and brake light; front and rear brakes; turn signals; a horn; and two mirrors.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best riding formation is generally:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group rides. Switch to single-file when turning, riding through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards and conditions.

questions.question: A helmeted rider is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider not wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash compared to riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane usually contains an oily strip. This part of the lane is:

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of traffic lanes. The road provides enough traction for safe riding unless it is wet. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often ride around it while staying in the center of the lane.

questions.question: A passenger on a motorcycle should:

options.text: Mount the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Mount the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as close to the rear of the motorcycle as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mount the motorcycle after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Passengers should get on after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: As an operator, you should prepare a passenger to ride by instructing them to do each of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to: mount only after the engine starts, sit as far forward as possible without crowding you, hold onto the handholds or your waist/hips/belt, and keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: To accommodate a passenger, you may have to:
questions.explanation: A passenger's weight affects your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks before carrying a passenger. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: When may you not need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When there is a lot of traffic
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle takes longer to stop than normal. Increase distance if pavement is slippery, you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: A larger cushion of space may not be necessary if:

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead of you.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions are not perfect. Add distance if pavement is slippery, you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left part of the lane
The center part of the lane
The right part of the lane
Either the left or right part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left part of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out from between cars, and cars pulling out of spaces.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may tempt the driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: If the road is wet, you should avoid:

options.text: The left part of the lane
The center part of the lane
The right part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center part of the lane
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of the lane. This strip loses traction when wet. You can ride to the side of the strip and still stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is good because the driver will see you easily
Is not safe because drivers rarely check their side mirrors
Is good because a passenger may tell the driver you are there
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not safe because drivers rarely check their side mirrors
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane when following a car so the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, you should adjust the:
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the weight you are carrying.
